title: Finite limits and colimits of finite etale covers
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme. Then $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ has finite limits and
finite colimits, and for every morphism $Y'\to Y$ the base change functor
is exact.

proof.text: In $\mathsf{FEt}(Y)$ every map $P\to R$ is finite (the composite to $Y$ is finite and $R\to Y$ is separated) and etale by cancellation. The identity of $Y$ is finite etale and terminal. Scheme pullbacks $P\times_R Q$ remain finite etale over $Y$: their projection to $Q$ is a base change of $P\to R$, and composition preserves both properties. Their universal property restricts to this full subcategory.

For any $g:Y\prime\to Y$, the fibre-product universal property identifies $g^*Y$ with $Y\prime$ and $g^*(P\times_R Q)$ with $g^*P\times_{g^*R}g^*Q$, preserving all projections: both represent compatible maps to $P,Q,Y\prime$. The terminal-and-pullback criterion gives finite limits and their preservation.

Finite coproducts are scheme disjoint unions. They are finite by binary finite-coproduct stability and induction, and etale by finite-coproduct stability. The empty scheme is finite since its affine algebra is the zero finite module, and etale vacuously on source charts. Their scheme universal property restricts to maps over $Y$; the coproduct base-change isomorphism shows $g^*$ preserves them, including the empty one.

Given $a,b:Z\rightrightarrows P$, apply the local normal-form lemma to this finite diagram. It supplies an etale covering $U_i\to Y$ on which $P,Z$ are copies of $U_i$ indexed by finite sets $S_i,T_i$, and both arrows are induced by fixed functions $\alpha_i,\beta_i:T_i\to S_i$.

Put $E_i=S_i/{\sim}$, where $\sim$ is generated by $\alpha_i(t)\sim\beta_i(t)$, and $Q_i=\coprod_{E_i}U_i$. This is finite etale by step 3. Define $q_i$ by $s\mapsto[s]$. A map $P_{U_i}\to H$ over $U_i$ is a family of sections $h_s$; it equalizes the arrows exactly when $h_{\alpha_i(t)}=h_{\beta_i(t)}$. Equality propagates along the generated equivalence relation, giving one and only one section for each class, hence a unique factor through $q_i$. After any $V\to U_i$, finite-coproduct base change gives the same index maps on copies of $V$, so the identical argument applies.

Apply universal-coequalizer descent to these $q_i$. It gives a finite etale $Q\to Y$ and $q:P\to Q$ whose pullback along every $Y\prime\to Y$ is a coequalizer among all schemes over $Y\prime$, hence also among finite etale ones. Uniqueness of coequalizers identifies any other choice with this one compatibly with its quotient map. Thus every base change preserves coequalizers.
The coproduct-and-coequalizer criterion now gives finite colimits and their preservation by $g^*$. Together with step 2 this is exactness, meaning preservation of finite limits and finite colimits.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme. Then $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ has finite limits,
computed as in $Y$-schemes; it has finite coproducts, the initial object
being the empty scheme and the coproduct of $P$ and $Q$ the disjoint
union $P\amalg Q$; it has quotients $P/G$ by finite groups $G$ acting on
$P$ over $Y$; and every monomorphism in $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ is the
inclusion of a direct summand, i.e. of an open and closed subscheme.

proof.text:
Step 1: finite limits. With $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ as in
[def-galois-categories] and the scheme-theoretic fibre products of
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], the final object is $Y$, and fibre
products of finite etale $Y$-schemes are finite etale over $Y$, since
finite etale morphisms are stable under base change and composition and
a morphism between finite etale $Y$-schemes is itself finite etale.
Hence $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ is closed under finite limits in
$Y$-schemes.
Step 2: finite coproducts. The empty scheme and disjoint unions of
finite etale $Y$-schemes are finite etale over $Y$, and they are the
initial object and the coproducts in $Y$-schemes.
Step 3: quotients by finite groups. Let a finite group $G$ act on $P$ by
$Y$-automorphisms. Over an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $Y$ the
preimage of $V$ in $P$ is $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ finite etale
over $R$, and $\operatorname{Spec}A^G$ is finite etale over $R$, its
formation commuting with flat base change, in particular with passing to
smaller affine opens. These affine quotients glue to a finite etale
$Y$-scheme $P/G$, and the universal property of $A^G$ among
$G$-invariant maps gives the universal property of the quotient.
Step 4: monomorphisms. A monomorphism $X\to Z$ in
$\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ is a monomorphism of schemes (its diagonal is an
isomorphism, fibre products being computed in schemes), and a flat
monomorphism locally of finite presentation is an open immersion. It is
also finite, hence closed, so its image is open and closed, and $Z$ is
the disjoint union of $X$ and the complementary open and closed
subscheme.
